reader.decision: Approve: change `hold_seats` to take the open `conn` and update `checkout` to pass it. Do not add the semaphore.
reader.decision_reason: The message traces the freeze to a nested pool acquire in one pod, where 10 holders each wait for a second connection. Passing `conn` removes that cause and puts both writes in one transaction. The semaphore only hides the nested pattern, and the message gives no sign that `hold_seats` must keep its own transaction.

reconstruction.problem: `checkout` holds one pool connection (`max_size=10`), then `hold_seats` calls `pool.connection()` for a second. When 10 requests in one pod each hold a connection, all 10 wait for a second one that no one can release. The other requests wait behind them. After the 30 second timeout, all of them fail with `PoolTimeout`.
reconstruction.what_breaks: During the 24 October Halden Arena on-sale, `checkout-api-2` had `in_flight=14`. Checkout froze for about 30 seconds, then all 14 requests returned 500. The next waiters deadlocked the same way and failed at 19:01:02. The database was idle at 38 of 200 connections. At normal traffic `in_flight=3`, so spare connections exist and nothing breaks. There is also a second bug: the seat hold commits on its own connection, so a later failure rolls back the order but leaves the seats held for 10 minutes.
reconstruction.fix: Change `hold_seats(event_id, seat_ids)` to `hold_seats(conn, event_id, seat_ids)`, run the seat `UPDATE` through `conn.execute`, and drop the `pool` import in `app/seats.py`. Change line 12 of `app/checkout.py` to pass `conn`. Order and seat writes then share one transaction and one connection.
reconstruction.cost: A signature change to `hold_seats`. The message found `checkout` to be the only caller in `app/`, but it did not check outside `app/`.

follow_up_questions: Does anything outside `app/` (scripts, jobs, tests) call `hold_seats`?
reader.closing_answer: Change `hold_seats` to take the open `conn` and update `checkout` to pass it. Skip the semaphore. Before you merge, grep the whole repo for other `hold_seats` callers, not just `app/`.
